chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf, from Muthanna al-Hannat, from Hatim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:
"If the man wishes, he frees his Umm al-Walad (concubine who bore him a child) and makes her manumission equivalent to her dowry."

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Umm al-Walad: A female slave who has given birth to her master's child.

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for freeing an Umm al-Walad and how is her manumission valued?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the financial mechanism of manumission for an 'Umm al-Walad', establishing that the master's voluntary act of freeing her is legally valued at the amount of her dowry (mahr). This ruling highlights the intersection of family law and slavery in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the dignity of the mother-child bond and providing a clear metric for compensation or debt settlement in case of disputes.
